//: CHANCE: THE PEOPLE OF THE REACH CROSSING YOUR PATH (docs/events/chance.md). Meetings bound by who a person is (a classmate by cohort, an old enemy by the engine's old_enemy mark, a rich house by wealth, a house with no world by holding, a young one of a lesser house by age, rank and wealth, a veteran by track, rank and age, two guests by the feud's blood_on_their_hands and the regard of the dead person's house). Threads: words_at_the_feast marks a guest quarrel_with_you, read by the_quarrel_comes_to_a_head (whose killing opens a blood debt, docs/FEUD.md); a_classmate_in_the_city or a_house_without_lands marks someone owes_you_a_favour, read by a_favour_repaid; a_merchant_princes_venture marks the merchant staked_by_you, read by the_venture_comes_home or the_venture_goes_down; a_patron_wanted marks a young person your_protege, read by the_one_you_stood_for. Every second step clears its mark. No Core marks: all the hooks are the engine's own.

effects.text: {self.name} put in a word for {classmate.name}, a cadet of the same year. It will be remembered.
{self.name} and {classmate.name} brought the cadets of their year together for a dinner, and the city noticed how many of them had risen.
{self.name} heard a good deal about {classmate.house} from {classmate.name}, who noticed how closely {self.name} listened.
{self.name} and {classmate.name} swore the friendship of their year again, and meant it.
{self.name} crossed the room and offered {enemy.name} a hand. After all those years, {enemy.name} took it.
{self.name} held {enemy.name}'s eye across the room until {enemy.name} looked away.
{self.name} left early, before {enemy.name} could make anything of the evening.
{self.name} had someone stand near {enemy.name} all evening, and heard most of what was said.
{envious.name} of {envious.house} made a joke of {self.name}'s house at a feast, and {self.name} laughed with the room.
{envious.name} of {envious.house} made a joke of {self.name}'s house at a feast. {self.name}'s answer was the one the room repeated.
{self.name} sent to {envious.name} of {envious.house} the morning after the feast. It was not an apology that came back.
{self.name} sent {envious.name} of {envious.house} a gift and a letter, and the quarrel between them was let go.
{self.name} met {envious.name} of {envious.house} with blades before witnesses, and drew first blood. The quarrel ended there.
{envious.name} of {envious.house} is dead, and nobody in the Reach doubts on whose word.
{self.name} let {envious.name} of {envious.house} talk. The talk went on, and so did the bad feeling.
{veteran.name} of {veteran.house} told {self.name} how the old battles were won, and {self.name} listened.
{veteran.name} of {veteran.house} speaks well of {self.name} in the wardrooms now, and the wardrooms listen.
{self.name} asked {veteran.name} of {veteran.house} to join the household.
{self.name} spent a long evening with {veteran.name}, and went home the better for it.
{self.name} stands at the centre of the great canvas in the public hall. {sitter.name} of {sitter.house} stands to one side.
{self.name} stands on the great canvas where the painter put them, among the rest.
{self.name} and {sitter.name} of {sitter.house} stand side by side on the great canvas, as equals, which surprised the city.
On the great canvas in the public hall, {sitter.name} of {sitter.house} is small, and at the back. {sitter.name} knows why.
{self.name} put 800 credits into a venture of {grandee.name} of {grandee.house}.
{self.name}'s name is on the charter of a venture of {grandee.house}, for a fee.
{grandee.name} of {grandee.house} showed {self.name} how a venture is put together.
{self.name} declined a share in a venture of {grandee.name} of {grandee.house}.
The venture of {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} came home, and {self.name} took 1,200 credits from it.
The venture of {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} came home. {self.name} took a share and a place at their table.
{self.name} took back what was put into the venture of {grandee.house}, and gave the profit to the city's poor.
{self.name} wrote off the 800 credits put into the venture of {grandee.name} of {grandee.house}, and did not press them.
{self.name} pressed {grandee.name} of {grandee.house} for the money lost in their venture, and had 300 credits of it.
{self.name} took what was owed by {grandee.house} in goods and paper, and had 500 credits of it.
{self.name} lent {claimant.name} of {claimant.house} 300 credits, and asked for nothing back yet.
{self.name} asked {claimant.name} of {claimant.house} to join the household.
{self.name} had a kind word for {claimant.name} of {claimant.house}, and nothing more.
{self.name} turned {claimant.name} of {claimant.house} away at the door.
{debtor.name} of {debtor.house} will pay what they owed {self.name} with their house's voice: {debtor.house} owes your house a vote.
{debtor.name} of {debtor.house} paid {self.name} 400 credits, and the favour was settled.
{self.name} told {debtor.name} of {debtor.house} that it had never been a debt.
{self.name} told {debtor.name} of {debtor.house} to keep the favour for another day.
{self.name} bought a secret about {subject.name} of {subject.house}, and has kept it, for the day it is wanted.
What {subject.name} of {subject.house} had done is known now, and {subject.house} is the less for it. {subject.name} knows who told.
{self.name} bought a secret about {subject.name} of {subject.house} and sent it to them, unread.
{self.name} sent away someone who had a secret to sell.
What {subject.name} of {subject.house} had done is known now, and {subject.house} is the less for it. {subject.name} knows who told.
{subject.house} paid {self.name} 400 credits for what {self.name} knew of {subject.name}, and had the proof back.
{self.name} burned what was known of {subject.name} of {subject.house}, and told them so.
{self.name} and {envoy.name} of {envoy.house} came to an understanding, with nothing written down.
{envoy.house} paid {self.name} 300 credits to mend things between the houses, and did not like paying it.
{self.name} let it be known that {envoy.name} of {envoy.house} had come asking.
{self.name} heard {envoy.name} of {envoy.house} out, and promised nothing.
{self.name} put their name behind {young.name} of {young.house}, who had nothing else to start with.
{self.name} asked {young.name} of {young.house} to join the household as a protégé.
{self.name} wrote a letter for {young.name} of {young.house}.
{self.name} had no time for {young.name} of {young.house}.
{self.name} and {risen.name} of {risen.house} swore friendship. They stand by each other now.
{self.name} called on {risen.name} of {risen.house} for what was owed, and had it.
{self.name} asked nothing of {risen.name} of {risen.house}, and the city said so.
{self.name} gave the place of honour to {guest.name} of {guest.house}. {other_guest.name} of {other_guest.house} left early.
{self.name} gave the place of honour to {other_guest.name} of {other_guest.house}, over {guest.name} of {guest.house}.
{self.name} seated {guest.name} and {other_guest.name} at opposite ends of the table. Neither was pleased.
At {self.name}'s table, {guest.name} of {guest.house} and {other_guest.name} of {other_guest.house} spoke civilly to each other for the first time in years.
